verdict.rationale: LaunchDarkly's own API access token docs say tokens can be scoped to restrict the operations they can perform, with a read-only integration as the example. That is first-party support for least-privilege credentials, but the evidence is a single thin statement and never ties these tokens to agent use. missing for 10: documentation of how fine-grained the scoping is (per-resource, per-project or per-environment), evidence that scoped tokens are used to authenticate agents such as MCP server or CLI clients, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can issue scoped/least-privilege API credentials for an agent

citations.quote: You can scope your API tokens to restrict the set of operations they can perform. For example, you can build an integration that only has read access
